supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:24 UTC, the domain controller recorded creation of the alerted account helpdesk2, attributed in the event to ali.hassan.

At 13:45:34 UTC, helpdesk2 was added to the Administrators group. This conflicts with the stated practice that temporary help-desk accounts are added only to Externals and never receive administrator rights.

Shortly before the account creation, ali.hassan logged on interactively to WS-NKIM-01 from 198.51.100.201. The inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-AHASSAN-01, so this observed session does not match the documented practice.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy logs for the proxy sensor were not collected from 13:30 to 14:20 UTC due to an outage, limiting visibility into web activity during the review window.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish whether the person ali.hassan authorized the account creation or whether the credentials were used by someone else.
The evidence does not establish whether there was an approved exception or change authorizing helpdesk2 or its Administrators membership.
The evidence does not establish whether the suspicious scheduled task on WS-NKIM-01 was related to the account creation.
additional_evidence_needed: Verify the account creation and privileged-group addition against approval records and interview the responsible administrator.
Correlate the domain-controller logon session for the account-management events with authentication and endpoint records to determine how ali.hassan's credentials were used.
Investigate the remote logon source and the WS-NKIM-01 scheduled task, including whether its encoded PowerShell command executed and what content it retrieved.
unrelated_findings: WS-NKIM-01 recorded creation of a scheduled task named Microsoft\Windows\HealthCheck by ali.hassan. Its hidden PowerShell command contains an encoded web request to http://198.51.100.201/a.ps1; the task's relationship to the alerted account creation is not established. Track separately. (T177-00066)
